name: Donors Trust

summary.text: DonorsTrust is a Virginia-based 501(c)(3) donor-advised fund established in 1999 by Whitney Ball and Kim Dennis to serve donors committed to limited government, personal responsibility and free enterprise; its affiliate Donors Capital Fund operates alongside it. Its Form 990 filings on ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer show revenue of $294 million and total assets of $1.36 billion for the fiscal year ending December 2024, and it says it has granted about $1.7 billion to more than 1,900 charities. Sociologist Robert Brulle's 2014 study of climate countermovement funding found that pass-through foundations including Donors Trust and Donors Capital Fund supplied a rapidly rising share of traceable foundation funding to those organisations as named funders such as Koch and ExxonMobil foundations pulled back.

facts.claim: DonorsTrust was established in 1999 as a 501(c)(3) public charity to ensure the intent of donors dedicated to the ideals of limited government, personal responsibility and free enterprise; its own tribute page names Kim Dennis and Whitney Ball as founders, with Dennis as board chair and Ball as founding president.

DonorsTrust describes its donor-advised accounts as offering tax treatment, flexibility and anonymity while avoiding the costs of private foundations, and says it has granted approximately $1.7 billion to more than 1,900 charities.

ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer summary of Donors Trust Inc's Form 990 filings (EIN 52-2166327) reports revenue of $294 million, expenses of $292 million and total assets of $1.36 billion for the fiscal year ending December 2024, with filings available from 2010 to 2024.

Robert Brulle's study 'Institutionalizing delay', published in Climatic Change (vol. 122, 2014), used IRS data and Foundation Center records to analyse 91 climate change countermovement organisations funded by 140 foundations between 2003 and 2010, finding an annual income of just over $900 million and an annual average of $64 million in identifiable foundation support, with the majority coming from conservative foundations.
facts.quote: an annual income of just over $900 million, with an annual average of $64 million in identifiable foundation support

facts.claim: Brulle's study found evidence of a trend toward concealing the sources of countermovement funding through donor-directed philanthropies, with funding routed through pass-through foundations such as Donors Trust and Donors Capital, whose funders cannot be traced, rising sharply as traceable funding from named foundations declined.
facts.quote: third party pass-through foundations like Donors Trust and Donors Capital, whose funders cannot be traced, has risen dramatically

facts.claim: Drexel University's press release on the study, as quoted by DeSmog, said Donors Trust provided about 25 percent of all traceable foundation funding used by organisations promoting denial of climate change by 2010, up from about 3 percent in 2003.
facts.quote: about 25% of all traceable foundation funding used by organizations engaged in promoting systematic denial of climate change

facts.claim: Grist reported, citing Donors Trust's 2010 Form 990, that the fund made a $7,577,000 grant that year to the Americans for Prosperity Foundation.

sources.title: How the Kochs funneled millions to climate deniers through a secretive nonprofit

facts.claim: DeSmog reports that grantees of Donors Trust and Donors Capital Fund have included the Competitive Enterprise Institute, the Heartland Institute and the Americans for Prosperity Foundation, and that Donors Trust itself states it takes no position on the science of human-caused climate change.

openQuestions: Site claim that funding 'shifted to anonymous routes such as Donors Trust and Donors Capital Fund' (Brulle 2014) is supported by the study's abstract and press release.

Site lobby-section claim that Donors Trust 'supplied about a quarter of traceable foundation money to the climate countermovement by 2010, up from 3% in 2003, as named Koch and Exxon giving fell' is supported by the Drexel press release as quoted by DeSmog; the 25 percent figure is a share of traceable foundation funding, not of all funding, and the owner may want to confirm it against the paper's tables.

No connection was recorded to the Koch network or ExxonMobil: Brulle's study reports their named foundation giving declined as pass-through giving rose, but does not state that either routed money through Donors Trust. Grist's 'Koch-linked intermediary' framing was not verified.

Grantees named by DeSmog and Grist (Americans for Prosperity Foundation, Heartland Institute, Competitive Enterprise Institute) are not entity ids on the site, so no connections were recorded; grant-level detail is in Schedule I of each Form 990 on ProPublica.

A separate ProPublica entry (EIN 26-2515785) titled 'Donors Trust' shows negligible figures and is probably a different organisation; the site alias 'Donors Capital Fund' has its own EIN and filings, which were not retrieved.
